Behold, gentlemen! An actually plausible and viable romance that could work in the real world, but done in an anime. Love is more than just a sappy 'I love you,' it is also about making sacrifices so that you can support each other. Given that this arc is about high school students, the sacrifices obviously revolve around school and studies getting the way of quality time.

This is why I enjoy Nanasaki Ai's arc so much more than the others; because it plays the world as being a bit grittier and a bit more real. While all of the themes here are real, this right here is the story you could hear being told by someone with a straight face as to how they met their partner.

And frankly, I find it disappointing that as amazing an arc as this was, that there are not many fictional romances -- either in anime, manga, light novels, visual novels, or even western media -- that really come as close to the bare truth and honesty as this arc. This is it. This is the peak. This is romance as it presently exists.

Truth. I had no idea I needed glasses for a long time. Part of it was sheer dumb luck, and part of it was my parents being my parents and not getting me damn tested. Turns out I am a damn bat!

On the flipside, and I don't know how common this is, but I have excellent close-up vision. I didn't realize this was a thing until I started printing out things to read in class in font size 6 to save printer paper and help with privacy. Then I moved to 4, and stuck with it. I can actually usually read microprint, if I can get close to it.

I guess if I wasn't killed in the past, and just stuck with being a wife, I'd probably make an excellent detail-work craftsman. I have good dexterity, so I'd be great with intense detail. Downside is I'm also a lefty! That would've gone over like a lead balloon.

I've apparently been nearsighted since I was at least in grade school. When I was in 6th grade, I had laser eye surgery to correct a lazy eye, but a consequence was that it would make me more nearsighted than I already was. I still had no idea how bad my vision was. When I had the choice, I always sat up front in classrooms because it just always made me concentrate better. I didn't actually notice until one day I went to school with my contacts in and a whole new world opened up for me. It was insane what the difference was between a doctor's office and the real world.

Nearsightedness was far more rare in the past. It's growth is tied to changes in spending most time outdoors looking at objects of varying distances, to spending most of our time indoors looking at near-focus objects (books, computer screens, etc).

Sharp vision is not terribly important from an evolutionary standpoint. If you could see animals well enough to kill them and eat them thats ll you needed.

Now we need to read and see fine closeup details so it more important now.

I was wondering this the other day. I was a really active kid and didn't spend much time inside when almost overnight my eyesight went to shit. Basically before glasses were invented, I'd probably be dead as fuck. I wouldn't be able to hunt or gather. I can't read a book unless it's less than 6 inches from my face. I'd really just be considered blind, so I'd do whatever blind people did back then. I guess I am fortunate to be born when I was, although I wouldn't mind being born later to ensure I'm eligible for eye surgery.
